sentences.text: This dinosaur featured a massive bony frill, three prominent skull horns, and a large body supported on four legs.
Its sturdy frame included strong limbs, short hands with three hooves, and short feet ending in four hooves.
The largest known skull, identified as specimen MWC 7584, measured 2.5 meters in length when complete.
The animal's skin was covered in large basement scales that reached up to 9 centimeters across.
Triceratops was a giant creature, growing to lengths of 8 to 9 meters and weighing between 6 and 10 metric tons.
One specific individual named Kelsey measured between 22 and 24 feet long with a skull spanning 6.5 feet.
Another famous specimen known as Big John was estimated to be 26.1 feet long and 10 feet tall.
The fossilized skin of a specimen named Lane was preserved through a unique process called clay templating.
This species holds the title of official state fossil for South Dakota and official state dinosaur for Wyoming.
The genus was first described in 1889 by the American paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh.
The initial fossil specimen attributed to the group was discovered by George Lyman Cannon near Denver, Colorado, in the spring of 1887.
Between 1889 and 1891, John Bell Hatcher collected thirty-one additional skulls for the scientific record.

These herbivores primarily consumed low-growing vegetation but could potentially knock down taller plants using their horns, beak, and bulk.

While certainly quadrupedal, there is debate regarding its posture, with some believing its front legs sprawled at a considerable angle to support the head's weight.

The first extensive ontogenetic study of Triceratops was published in the journal Proceedings of the Royal Society in 2006.
Triceratops is classified as a genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsian dinosaur.
T. horridus is the type species of Triceratops, originally described as Ceratops by Marsh in 1889.
Thomas Lehman defined the subfamilies in 1990 and diagnosed Triceratops as a ceratopsine based on several morphological features.
Triceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
It lived approximately 69 to 66 million years ago during the late Maastrichtian age.
Triceratops lived in environments consisting of floodplains and inland forests.
Isotopic analysis suggests Triceratops specimens from the Darnell Triceratops Bonebed likely inhabited freshwater floodplains, though they were probably not restricted to a single environment.

There is an ongoing debate regarding the function of Triceratops' frill and horns, with traditional views favoring defense against predators and recent interpretations suggesting roles in species identification, courtship, and dominance displays.
In 1986, John Ostrom and Peter Wellnhofer proposed that all Triceratops remains belong to a single species, T. horridus.
Researchers suggest it is unlikely that the nipple-like projections on Triceratops feature scales bore bristles, unlike those found in other ceratopsians.
Torosaurus is distinguished by an elongated skull and two oval openings in its frill.
